tei:div.tei:p: This earth pledge by Carol T. Gaddy and Marianne Wolfman-Dawn is included in a short essay by Gaddy entitled “Our New Pledge of Allegiance.” The essay can be found in What Will It Take to Prevent Nuclear War: Grassroots Responses to Our Most Challenging Question (ed. Pat Farren 1983), p. 149. Carol Gaddy writes that the pledge “was composed spontaneously by me and Marianne Wolfman-Dawn as we marched on the road to Damascus, Arkansas, April 25, 1981, protesting the nuclear missile site where a Titan missile had exploded the previous November, endangering the people it was meant to protect.” A photo of this march showing Carol Gaddy and Marianne Wolfman-Dawn was published on the cover of Ours: a Feminist Newspaper (vol. 3, no. 5, Little Rock, Arkansas- Winter 1980). (Many thanks to the University of Arkansas at Little Rock Center for Arkansas History and Culture for digitizing and exhibiting this newspaper cover.)

As attested by Bryna Fireside and Elaine Lytel, this earth pledge was cited at the opening ceremonies of The Women’s Encampment for a Future of Peace and Justice in Romulus, New York on 4 July 1983 (in The Women’s Encampment for a Future of Peace and Justice: Images and Writings (1987), p. 21).
